en.title: Players Who Can Beat Every Opponent in Three Rounds
en.description:
Each player has three distinct boost values, each used once per match. X can beat Y if there exist arrangements of both players' values such that X is strictly greater than Y in at least two rounds. Count the players who can beat every other player individually; different opponents may use different arrangements.

The standard I/O and the solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n (2..100000), followed by n lines of three boost values (1..10^9); values within a line are distinct, and values may repeat across lines.
en.explanation: Example 1: each side has a pairing that wins two rounds, so the answer is 2. Example 2: only the second player can beat the first, so the answer is 1. Example 3: each player's middle value exceeds every minimum and each maximum exceeds every middle value, so all three players win; the answer is 3.
hints: Sort each player's values as a<b<c; a player can beat another if their own b is greater than the other's a and their own c is greater than the other's b. So precompute the maximum of all a and of all b, then filter.
